[BLOCKING] `orders/reports.py`, `kitchen_summary`: it buckets orders with `o.created_at.date()`. `created_at` is timezone-aware UTC (`models.py:48`). The `london_day` docstring says kitchens report in London time, and `daily_revenue` already uses `london_day`. During British Summer Time, an order created at 23:30 UTC on 1 June is 00:30 on 2 June in London. This function counts it under 1 June, so one day's orders and revenue are understated and the next day's are overstated. The function returns normally and nothing signals the error. It also disagrees with `daily_revenue` for the same orders. Fix: compare `london_day(o.created_at) == day`.

[NIT] The function filters on `created_at`, not delivery time. An order created late one day and delivered the next is counted on the creation day. This matches `daily_revenue`, so it is probably intended, but the "delivered orders for a day" wording is ambiguous.
